programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Liz McIvor explores the heritage of our canal network. After years of decline in the postwar period, much of the network was eventually restored. Once places of labour and industry, they became places of leisure and tranquillity. The newly renovated canals were increasingly popular for boating holidaymakers. Liz visits the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct in Wales and travels to Birmingham, where canals have become catalysts for property development and urban regeneration. Canals offer so many benefits today. Perhaps, Liz suggests, it is time to construct a few more?

programme.title: The Lakes with Paul Rose
programme.desc: Remote Eskdale is the final destination in explorer Paul Rose's trek through the Lake District. This corner of the western Lakes is off the normal tourist track, but it boasts England's highest mountain. Before heading for the tough Lakeland summit of Scafell Pike, Paul meets the folk who run one of the country's most scenic railways, he has a close encounter with a vulture and gets to grips with the locals in a spot of Cumberland wrestling.

programme.title: The Human Body: Secrets of Your Life Revealed
programme.desc: Over your lifetime, you undergo an extraordinary change - no other animal on earth goes through such a dramatic metamorphosis. In this programme, Chris and Xand van Tulleken explore the latest understanding of how we all grow. They look at the reason our childhood lasts longer than that of any other creature on earth and reveal the communities of microbes - our microbiome - that we cultivate throughout our lives. They also uncover the mysterious trigger for our transformation from child to adult and, for the first time, show the remarkable spark of life that is emitted when sperm and egg first meet.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Liz McIvor discovers how carving up the landscape in order to build canals helped further our understanding of the earth below. The canal builders struggled with rocks. Without maps or geological surveys, construction often relied on guesswork. The Kennet and Avon had more than its fair share of problems. William Smith, a surveyor working on the connecting Somerset Coal Canal, discovered a way of ordering layers of rocks. He eventually created the first geological map of England and Wales - the so-called 'map that changed the world'.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: The village of Milton Abbas in Dorset perfectly captures our romantic notion of what the idyllic English village should look like. But as archaeologist Ben Robinson reveals, behind it lurks a history of one man's wealth and power. With help from local historians, Ben learns how the local landowner in the 18th century destroyed a nearby town, uprooting its residents, because it ruined the view from his house. The landscape was transformed and a new village was built as part of his showpiece estate.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Using years of BBC history archive film, Dr Alice Roberts explores how our views and understanding of Roman Britain have changed and evolved over the decades. Along the way she investigates a diverse range of subjects from the Roman invasion, through Hadrian's Wall, the Vindolanda tablets and the eventual collapse of Roman rule. Drawing on the work of archaeologists and historians throughout the decades, Alice uncovers how and why our views of this much-loved period of our history have forever been in flux.

programme.title: The Lost Libraries of Timbuktu
programme.desc: Aminatta Forna tells the story of legendary Timbuktu and its long-hidden legacy of hundreds of thousands of ancient manuscripts. With its university founded around the same time as Oxford, Timbuktu is proof that the reading and writing of books have long been as important to Africans as they are to Europeans.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Liz McIvor discovers how carving up the landscape in order to build canals helped further our understanding of the earth below. The canal builders struggled with rocks. Without maps or geological surveys, construction often relied on guesswork. The Kennet and Avon had more than its fair share of problems. William Smith, a surveyor working on the connecting Somerset Coal Canal, discovered a way of ordering layers of rocks. He eventually created the first geological map of England and Wales - the so-called 'map that changed the world'.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: The village of Milton Abbas in Dorset perfectly captures our romantic notion of what the idyllic English village should look like. But as archaeologist Ben Robinson reveals, behind it lurks a history of one man's wealth and power. With help from local historians, Ben learns how the local landowner in the 18th century destroyed a nearby town, uprooting its residents, because it ruined the view from his house. The landscape was transformed and a new village was built as part of his showpiece estate.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Using years of BBC history archive film, Dr Alice Roberts explores how our views and understanding of Roman Britain have changed and evolved over the decades. Along the way she investigates a diverse range of subjects from the Roman invasion, through Hadrian's Wall, the Vindolanda tablets and the eventual collapse of Roman rule. Drawing on the work of archaeologists and historians throughout the decades, Alice uncovers how and why our views of this much-loved period of our history have forever been in flux.

programme.desc: Janice Long presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 25 September 1986. Featuring Amazulu, Huey Lewis and the News, Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk, Genesis, Loose Ends, The Communards and Run DMC.

programme.title: Sting and The Police at the BBC
programme.desc: The late 1970s to mid 1980s was a period when, in terms of international success, every little thing The Police did was magic – with Sting, Andy Summers and Stewart Copeland enjoying a run of chart-topping singles, best-selling albums and huge concerts all across the world. When the trio went their separate ways in 1986, it was Sting who then became even more of a wanted man, establishing himself as one of the UK’s most respected singer-songwriters. This collection of performances from the BBC’s archives celebrates the solo star and the band that brought him to the world's attention in the first place, including the very best of both careers with hits like Roxanne, Fragile, Message in a Bottle, Brand New Day and Every Breath You Take.

programme.title: Reel Stories
programme.desc: Multi-award-winning artist Sting joins Dermot O’Leary for an in-depth interview about his remarkable life and career. From his very first TV appearance on The Old Grey Whistle Test in 1978, to performing at Live Aid in 1985, to his reunion tour with the Police in 2007, Sting’s career has been well documented on screen. The appearances are so numerous that there is much he hasn’t seen – until now. Prompted by this abundance of archive footage, Sting shares his memories and stories with Dermot and reminisces about his musical journey that now spans five decades.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: Moor Park, Preston plays host to Saturday’s headlining act at Radio 2 In The Park. Sting, who is fronting his new power rock trio, is fresh off the STING 3.0 tour. Sting, alongside long-time collaborator and guitarist Dominic Miller, and dynamic drummer Chris Maas of Mumford & Sons fame, will be performing a selection of music from Sting’s timeless discography, including solo hits, surprise rarities and of course, The Police classics.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The right of reply has long been a cornerstone of journalism, giving those involved in a story the chance to respond before publication. But with politicians and public figures now using social media to publish their own version first, is this principle being undermined? Guto Harri, former Downing Street director of communications, Professor Karen Fowler-Watt from City St George's, University of London, and journalist Matt Shea assess how the practice is changing. As streaming services compete for attention, TV remotes usually now include buttons for platforms such as Netflix and YouTube, often paid for by the services themselves. UK broadcasters argue this disadvantages British platforms and have called for a dedicated 'British' button. Technology historian Edd Thomas and Professor Catherine Johnson from the University of Leeds explain why the remote has become such a significant battleground.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Has the AI industry finally recognised the dangers of the technology it is building? A researcher leaves one of the world's leading AI companies with a warning that the race to build ever more powerful systems could end in human extinction. Days later, the chief executive of the same company calls for the industry to slow down. This episode, AI Decoded examines the growing debate over AI safety, regulation and control. From fears that advanced systems could outpace human understanding to concerns over cyberattacks, biological threats and the challenge of containing increasingly powerful models, we ask whether the world's AI companies are moving too fast, and whether anyone can agree on how to slow down. The discussion also explores AI 'kill switches', international oversight, the role of governments, and whether rivalry between the United States and China makes meaningful cooperation impossible.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate how the 1990s fashion for bamboo in our gardens is causing expensive problems for some homeowners 25 years later and what can be done to stop the plant from running riot under your property. And the man who narrowly escaped injury when the glass roof of his conservatory shattered. Who should foot the bill with the installer out of business?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: We welcome back two developers who’ve been on the show before. One is tackling a big end-of-terrace in north London, whereas the other seems to have nabbed a bargain in Suffolk. Martel also checks out an interesting property in Morecambe with beautiful sea views.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross is in South Yorkshire, where he meets rocking horse collector, designer and restorer Anthony Dew. They chat about the long history of the toys right back to the very first rocking horse, said to have been made for King Charles I when he was a child back in 1605. In Elsecar, two teams gallop around an antiques centre with their experts David Harper and Izzie Balmer, trying to find three items each to sell at auction. The red team, brother and sister-in-law Julian and Debbie, can’t stop picking up pottery. Meanwhile, father and daughter-in-law Andrew and Tammy spy some military goggles, but can they be sure how old they are? Auctioneer Sean Devitt is on the rostrum in Derby, but can he deliver a profit for the teams?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Mark Wright, extreme cleaner Maxine Dwyer and expert fixer Derek Nesbeth help Alison, who has been juggling a busy career with caring for her parents. Her kitchen is overflowing with baking equipment for her home business, and a spare room has become a catch-all space she can no longer use. Maxine restores order with deep cleaning and smart organisation in the kitchen, while Mark and Derek rework the spare room into a dual-purpose guest bedroom and home office, complete with bespoke storage and a revamped desk.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Greek Job
programme.desc: Inspired by Gerald Durrell’s love of wildlife, Amanda and Alan design their first ever children’s bedroom and visit Gerald’s widow Lee for inspiration.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s all action in Cornwall as Jules Hudson teams up with two fitness fanatics from the town of Hertford, who are searching for their perfect seaside escape. They are after space for a home pottery studio, with a gym close by, and Jules has lined up some classic Cornish gems to get their hearts racing. The competition heats up even more when they all take to the water at Padstow for a spot of gig boat racing.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Frances are in Chester to help Lyn transform her overgrown garden, plagued with nettles, dead bushes, broken slabs and a bare patch where a shed once stood, into a Mediterranean-inspired darts sanctuary. Lyn dreams of a tranquil, low-maintenance space with room for chairs and a table, where she can unwind and play darts, while also creating a haven for family gatherings with her family and grandchildren. After facing heartbreaking losses and challenges over the past few years – including the deaths of her husband and mother-in-law, and redundancy from her accounting job, Lyn has remained resilient thanks to the support of her sister Karen. Can the team turn her chaotic plot into the ultimate darts-friendly Mediterranean retreat on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: All aboard the Antiques Express! Dealers Danny Sebastian and Roo Irvine steam into Cheshire and the West Midlands on the third leg of their adventure together. Expect trains, high-speed shopping and a spot of spotting. Scouring the shops, Roo comes across a find from her homeland, with tartan and thistles aplenty, and takes time for an item that would grace any art deco mantelpiece. Danny’s excitement is stoked by a bit of brass with an added extra and a heavyweight item with a flavour of seaside entertainment. Then it’s down the track to Crewe, the epicentre of all things locomotive, where our pair grab their jotters and discover the appeal and surprising history of a much-maligned pastime. This service terminates at a saleroom in Glasgow. Will Roo’s Scottish discovery serve up a profit? Or will Danny’s doorstop be 'the way to do it'?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Michael Ball. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: Byron faces their toughest challenge yet as they begin their sentence in a young offender institute. As the days and weeks pass, Byron feels increasingly isolated and shut out from the outside world. They keep their head down but soon become the target of bullies. With nowhere to hide, Byron must somehow find a way to survive. They receive a possible lifeline when they learn that with good behaviour, and committing to further education, they stand a chance of an early release. Byron begins to settle into a steady rhythm and strikes up an expected friendship with an inmate who challenges Byron to confront their past decisions and take genuine responsibility for their actions. But when temptation and self-destructive impulses resurface, Byron must learn whether they can truly break free from their old patterns, stop the cycle of blame and finally accept accountability. But trapped within the confines of prison, is it too late to make a difference?

programme.title: What It Feels Like for a Girl
programme.desc: Newly released from prison and living authentically as a woman, Byron is determined to escape Hucknall once and for all. A humiliating university interview reveals the true scale of the challenge ahead of Byron – navigating life as a trans woman will not be easy, made even more complicated by her criminal record. Seeking reassurance and refuge, Byron attempts to rekindle her friendship with Lady Die and Sasha, only to find both girls have moved on with their lives. But when an unexpected ghost from Byron’s past emerges, she is forced to confront an unsettling truth: perhaps she is fighting a losing battle against her future, and Hucknall is where she truly belongs. Standing at the crossroads between her old life and an uncertain future, a devastating turn of events threatens to anchor Byron permanently to the very existence she has been desperate to leave behind.

programme.title: Back to the Future Part III
programme.desc: Stranded in 1955, Marty McFly learns about the death of Doc Brown in 1885 and must travel back in time to save him. With no fuel readily available for the DeLorean, Marty and Doc must figure out how to escape the Old West.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: An exclusive couples retreat turns deadly when the therapist is drowned at sea during her evening swim. When fingermarks are found on the victim’s neck, Mervin confirms foul play was involved, and suspicion soon shifts to her clients - two couples who have paid a small fortune to mend their fractured marriages. But all four were having dinner together at the time of the murder, and while each member of the party slipped away from the table for a few minutes, there is no way any of them could have drowned their therapist in the middle of the ocean and made it back in time... is there? Meanwhile, Mervin is determined to track down his brother, along with the possessions Solomon stole from him. But Mervin gets more than he bargained for when Solomon’s attempts to make amends land them in hot water. Is it the end of the road for the two belligerent brothers?

programme.title: Cunk on Life
programme.desc: Pioneering documentary maker Philomena Cunk returns with her most ambitious quest to date: venturing right up the universe and everything to examine life and existence in an attempt to find out the point of it all. Along the way, she interrogates experts on subjects from the big bang to biology and art to artificial intelligence. Really get to the nub of it. Mockumentary from Charlie Brooker, starring Diane Morgan.

programme.title: This Country
programme.desc: Kurtan is focusing his attentions on the annual village scarecrow festival, a key event in the village calendar that can both unite and divide the community. Tensions run high when his chances of winning the competition are compromised by being given a less than ideal plot to display his scarecrow. Meanwhile, Kerry faces a challenge to her authority.

programme.title: This Country
programme.desc: When Kerry's neighbour Mandy Harris starts a tattoo business, Kerry is delighted to be one of her first customers. Meanwhile, Kurtan fixates on trying to track down a long-lost school friend.

programme.title: This Country
programme.desc: This Country is a sitcom series for BBC Three which takes the mockumentary format to explore the lives of young people in modern rural Britain, focusing on cousins Kerry and Lee ‘Kurtan’ Mucklowe and their life experiences in a typical Cotswold village. Faith in the police is falling. This Country investigates how justice is viewed by Kerry and Kurtan, as they await the release from prison of their uncle, Steve ‘Nugget’ Nuggins, who they believe was wrongfully imprisoned for ‘having a laugh’.

programme.title: This Country
programme.desc: Kerry and Kurtan attend a talk at the village hall with a businesswoman who runs what may or may not be a pyramid scheme. Kerry is inspired and starts a career as a door-to-door saleswoman. However, her focus on the business leads to disharmony with Kurtan, and this is only compounded when he makes some new friends in the village.

programme.title: This Country
programme.desc: Kerry's father, Martin, is accused of being a peeping Tom. Meanwhile, Kurtan romantically pursues a girl who has just moved into the village, but he finds he has a rival for her affections in his friend Slugs.

programme.title: The Split Up
programme.desc: Aria Kishan, a leading divorce lawyer for Manchester’s elite, is poised to take the reins from her father, Dhruv, at Kishan Law, the family firm he founded after he moved to the UK from India years ago. She has big aspirations for the company, including moving away from their current premises and expanding at a new upmarket location. But Dhruv wonders if she can take on the responsibility of Kishan Law alone. Aria’s wedding preparations to steady long-term partner Neal have been paused following the tragic death of her mother, Raina, six months ago. Raina was sick, and Aria moved back in with Dhruv to help care for her and has stayed since to make sure her dad was managing. However, her family have decided Aria can’t put her life on hold any longer and decide to help by planning a surprise engagement party for her and Neal. This coincides with Luke, a secret former flame of Aria’s, arriving at the firm, and all of her well-formed plans for her future start to spiral out of control.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams heads to the north Yorkshire countryside with a £280,000 budget, helping Richard, Helen and her daughter Immi swap a busy Kentish town for the Yorkshire way of life. With Richard happiest on the water, and mum and daughter wanting a dedicated craft room, the property search serves up plenty of character, including a waterside mystery house with spectacular views. Briony also visits a vineyard, proving England’s wine country reaches further north than many might expect.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: It’s a rollercoaster ride as antiques dealers Roo Irvine and Danny Sebastian beat a path to Blackpool and beyond in their trusty steed, Felix, a 1963 Morris Traveller. Hitting the antiques shops of Lancaster, our pair unearth a whole hoard of treasures. Roo sets her sights on a bit of sparkle and goes glassy-eyed for a vase that reminds her of a seaside holiday sweet treat. Danny tries to carry away a hefty item that could be the start of someone’s publishing empire, and there's a box with a little touch of magic. Taking a cheeky wildlife break, our pair don their wellies and muck in with efforts to clear out invasive plants from a former quarry turned nature reserve to make space for its inhabitants. Then it’s off to auction to see if Roo’s bit of bling can enchant the saleroom or Danny’s magic box can conjure profits out of thin air.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Before boarding his train at Budapest’s historic Nyugati station, Michael Portillo explores its sumptuous royal waiting room, built specially for the Austro-Hungarian emperor Franz Joseph I and his empress, Elizabeth. Heading south, his next destination is the country’s third city of Szeged, close to the Serbian and Romanian borders. In the city’s historic centre, he finds the magnificent Great Synagogue, built in 1902, which reflects the size and prominence of Szeged’s Jewish population at that time. Just outside the city, on the banks of the River Tisza, Michael visits a region known for producing Hungary’s favourite spice, paprika, from ground red peppers. At a fourth-generation family farm, he tries a freshly picked pepper and joins the family for a hearty paprika stew.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the last leg of his journey, Michael Portillo arrives in the historic northern city of Eger. At its famous castle, he discovers how, during the 16th century, Ottoman invaders were defeated by a vastly outnumbered Hungarian force. It‘s a victory still celebrated to this day. Nearby, in the foothills of the Bükk Mountains, one of Hungary’s wine-producing areas, Michael takes a tour of a family-owned vineyard and samples the region’s signature wine, Bull’s Blood. Continuing east, his final destination is the Puszta, Hungary's largest national park, where animals have grazed for over 2,000 years. On a vast plain with endless skies, Michael is treated to an impressive display of horsemanship by Hungarian cowboys, called csikós.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Sara Pascoe welcomes 12 of Britain’s most talented home sewers into the sewing room, which is in an historic woollen mill on the outskirts of Leeds. Week One sees judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young ask them to create a capsule wardrobe consisting of three items. First, for the Pattern Challenge, they must produce a wool mini skirt with piped patch pockets. For the Transformation Challenge, the task is to turn lockdown loungewear into a going-out top for an adult, and in the Made to Measure, the sewers must perfectly fit a wrap dress to their model. One sewer gets off to a flying start, being awarded Garment of the Week, while another’s hopes are dashed as they become the first to be sent home.

programme.title: South Pacific
programme.desc: In the South Pacific there is no such thing as a deserted island. They may be the most isolated in the world, but every one of the region's 20,000 islands has been colonised, from New Guinea - home to birds of paradise and the tribe whose brutal initiation ceremony turns young warriors into 'crocodile' men - to Fiji, French Polynesia and Hawaii. This is the story of the ultimate castaways - from saltwater crocodiles and giant eels to crested iguanas and weird frogs - who succeeded against all odds to reach islands thousands of miles apart. These journeys are no mean feat. It has been estimated that an average of one species in every 60,000 years makes it to Hawaii. Incredibly, many of these colonisers made it to the islands thanks to some of the most violent forces of nature like cyclones and tsunamis. The voyages of the South Pacific's first people - the Polynesians - were no less remarkable. These journeys were some of the greatest acts of navigation ever undertaken, and they changed the nature of the South Pacific forever.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Muncaster Castle in Cumbria. Experts Caroline Hawley and James Lewis choose items to take to auction. James is drawn to a collection of WWI memorabilia and Caroline finds an exciting collection of postcards. Plus Paul meets an artist whose work has led him back in time to the ancient art of relief printing.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jennie Bond, James Bye, Kadeena Cox and Aurie Styla take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive heads to one of the Dominican Republic’s most northerly provinces, to the beautiful city of Puerto Plata. He learns about the incredible story of the Jewish refugees that found shelter in this country during World War II. He also discovers how to make the delicious plantain dish of mofongo, meets some of the finest merengue musicians in the country and heads to a busy banana farm, where he discovers a Dominican drink with a very racy reputation.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: TV presenter Charlotte Crosby and dancer Louie Spence take their friendship to a whole new level in the West Midlands. They're cosied up in an all-American muscle car, the Pontiac Trans Am, guided by experts Irita Marriott and Serhat Ahmet. Louie and Irita zero in on vintage lamps, garnitures and a sign that's as big as their personalities. Antiques virgin Charlotte opts for vintage toys, a spooky bible with hidden secrets and some art nouveau. There's enough time for a pit stop at a canine assault course for the dog-loving duo at the birthplace of Crufts. But can Louie behave well enough to stay off the obstacles? On this road trip, there's fun, laughter and frivolity, but will it all go to the dogs come auction time?

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: Paddy McGuinness visits a factory in Northern Ireland producing sausage rolls on an epic scale.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Will Young learns about his grandfather’s time as a prisoner of war in World War II. Delving further back, Will finds a connection to one of medieval history’s biggest villains and a king.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer tour the country's finest fishing spots and talk a lot of nonsense. Paul and Bob fish for barbel in Hay-on-Wye and sample the great outdoors.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories - reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world.

programme.title: The Devil’s Confession: The Lost Eichmann Tapes
programme.desc: Pressing forward with the prosecution, Hausner manages to secure a transcript of the Sassen Tapes, but the actual audio recordings continue to evade him. However, the information contained in the tapes may have repercussions for the new world order that emerges at the start of the Cold War, as well as Israel’s national interests.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: After five weeks of gruelling challenges, it's the Celebrity MasterChef final. Fifteen celebrities started the battle to become champion, and now only three remain. One of them will take the trophy - just one challenge stands between them and victory. The finalists must cook and present a faultless three-course meal for final judgement by Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli. It’s their last chance to prove they have what it takes, by showing true passion and creativity with their dishes. Who amongst this year’s finalists is the true cooking star and worthy of a place in the Celebrity MasterChef hall of fame? Only one can be crowned Celebrity MasterChef Champion 2026.

programme.title: The Split Up
programme.desc: Following the events of the engagement party, Aria is struggling to reach out to Maya. But there is plenty on her plate already, with the ripple effects of Dhruv’s shock announcement causing a rift between her and Neal, and throwing obstacles in her path for the Kishan Law move.

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: Reeling from their recent discovery, John and Lucy struggle to see how this new piece of information fits into what they already know. When a sushi bar turns into a crime scene, an unlikely witness helps John in both of his investigations. Desperate for answers to questions of his own, Russell takes matters into his own hands. But when a cryptic thumb drive is left behind by the witness and decoded by John, Russell is crushed by what he learns. Are some truths better left hidden?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Joe are in Alresford to help Sara and Jonny transform their overgrown, unloved plot into a Persian magic-meets-English countryside garden. The couple dream of a family-friendly space with cosy lounging spots, a chic dining area and a soft lawn where their little girl, Daphne, can play. To honour Sara’s Iranian heritage, they’d love Persian-inspired touches, from intricate tiling and archways to a striking tiled water feature, all balanced with the relaxed charm of the English countryside. Easy maintenance is a must, so the garden can be enjoyed, not laboured over. After a rollercoaster few years, leaving London for the calm of the countryside, saving for their dream home, welcoming Daphne, and facing career changes and challenges, Sara and Jonny are ready for a sanctuary that reflects their love and resilience. Can the team create their dream retreat for just £5,000?

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: All aboard the Antiques Express! Dealers Danny Sebastian and Roo Irvine steam into Cheshire and the West Midlands on the third leg of their adventure together. Expect trains, high-speed shopping and a spot of spotting. Scouring the shops, Roo comes across a find from her homeland, with tartan and thistles aplenty, and takes time for an item that would grace any art deco mantelpiece. Danny’s excitement is stoked by a bit of brass with an added extra and a heavyweight item with a flavour of seaside entertainment. Then it’s down the track to Crewe, the epicentre of all things locomotive, where our pair grab their jotters and discover the appeal and surprising history of a much-maligned pastime. This service terminates at a saleroom in Glasgow. Will Roo’s Scottish discovery serve up a profit? Or will Danny’s doorstop be 'the way to do it'?

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: In a special programme exploring the enduring value of allotment life, Frances Tophill heads to Exmouth in Devon, where thriving plots and passionate growers are at the heart of a vibrant community. At a time when more people want to know where their food comes from and enjoy the unbeatable taste of home-grown produce, Frances discovers why these much-loved spaces matter more than ever. Joe Swift heads to Manchester to offer advice to newbie allotmenteer De-Graft Mensah, who, when not presenting Newsround, can’t get enough of growing his own food. There’s a determined plot holder in Scarborough who refuses to let a pigeon-led brassica massacre get the better of her. And in Bradford, two allotment holders share how, for them, a love of growing has forged an unlikely friendship that bridges generations. And in a dramatic finale, actors Zoë Henry and Jeff Hordley - better known as Rhona Goskirk and Cain Dingle from Emmerdale - share the real-life soap opera behind their much-loved allotment and dig the dirt on who really does most of the work.

Sewing bespoke footwear means tackling a range of unfamiliar techniques, including punching eyelets and stitching soles - all of which must be done twice to create a perfect pair. The sewers need to be on the ball in the Transformation Challenge, converting old netball kits into a garment to wear off the court in just 90 minutes. For the Made-to-Measure Challenge, they each fit a jacket inspired by their sporting hero. As well as fit and finish, the judges will be looking to see if their hero’s personality or style is evident. Who will win garment of the week, and who will be last over the finish line?

programme.title: South Pacific
programme.desc: A large part of the remote, blue wilderness of the South Pacific is a marine desert. Many animals that live in the ocean - among them sharks, whales and turtles - must go to extraordinary lengths to survive. Tiger sharks travel hundreds of miles to feast on fledging albatross chicks and, every year, sperm whales journey from one side of the South Pacific to the other in their search for food and mates. Theirs is a journey that can end in tragedy. But the South Pacific is not all desert. New Zealand's super-rich coast supports huge pods of acrobatic dolphins; its coral reefs are some of the most diverse on earth; and there are few places richer in wildlife than the quirky Galapagos Islands, home to tropical penguins and surfing sea lions. Using the greatest shipwreck story of all time - an event that inspired Moby Dick - the huge challenges of survival in this seemingly endless blue ocean are revealed.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Sandon Hall in Staffordshire. Experts Christina Trevanion and David Fletcher choose items to take to auction, including a large collection of boxed Corgi toys and some rare watches. Presenter Paul Martin discovers the dramatic political life of one of Sandon's earlier owners, the 1st Earl of Harrowby, a member of William Pitt's cabinet, including a period as foreign secretary during the Napoleonic Wars.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: 26-year-old Kye is rushed into Resus suffering alcohol withdrawal seizures, but ED consultant Hazel is also concerned about an abscess on his arm that has failed to respond to treatment. Hazel questions Kye about his drug use and uncovers a possible cause for his resistance to antibiotics. She consults with the microbiology team, and in the meantime, begins a different treatment. After a motorbike crash, older couple Ken and Carol are brought into the emergency department, with Ken in extreme pain. Scans reveal six fractured ribs, putting 82-year-old Ken at high risk of serious complications. As anaesthetists work to control his pain and monitor his condition upstairs, his wife Carol, who was riding pillion and has fractured fingers herself, waits overnight on a chair in the emergency department. Elsewhere, trauma team leader Jules treats 88-year-old Lady Carole, who has fractured her leg while walking her dog in the garden. With her family at her side, the orthopaedic team must first stabilise the severe fracture with a plaster cast before she can undergo surgery.

programme.title: Wham! 10 Days in China
programme.desc: In 1985, Wham! made history as the first western pop act to perform in communist China. George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley travelled to Beijing and Guangzhou for a series of concerts that would make history. At a time when China was beginning to open to the wider world, their performances represented more than just entertainment - they were a rare cultural exchange and, for the audiences who attended, a first glimpse of western pop music performed live. Film-maker Lindsay Anderson had been commissioned to document the tour, but the project was fraught with challenges, leading to Anderson's dismissal. Though a version of the film was released, most of the footage was largely unseen. Using digitised archival footage alongside interviews with those who were there, this film presents a vivid portrait of a tour that has become legendary. It captures intimate moments behind the scenes, the nuanced political context, the excitement of the performances and the bizarre twists and turns of a true story that is stranger than fiction.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The Newbiggin crew race to the rescue of three children who have been swept out to sea on a small inflatable dinghy; the situation escalates when reports come in that the father has attempted to swim out to try to rescue them himself. In Selsey, a mayday comes in from a vessel taking on water in the English Channel; one of the casualties is reported to have suffered a head injury. On the Dorset coast, the Lyme Regis crew respond to reports of a couple cut off by a landslide on a notorious stretch of coast. And reports of two kite surfers struggling in the water put the Shoreham crew on red alert.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Frances are in Chester to help Lyn transform her overgrown garden, plagued with nettles, dead bushes, broken slabs and a bare patch where a shed once stood, into a Mediterranean-inspired darts sanctuary. Lyn dreams of a tranquil, low-maintenance space with room for chairs and a table, where she can unwind and play darts, while also creating a haven for family gatherings with her family and grandchildren. After facing heartbreaking losses and challenges over the past few years – including the deaths of her husband and mother-in-law, and redundancy from her accounting job, Lyn has remained resilient thanks to the support of her sister Karen. Can the team turn her chaotic plot into the ultimate darts-friendly Mediterranean retreat on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Roo Irvine and Danny Sebastian roll into Northamptonshire in Felix, their faithful vintage Morris Traveller, hunting for antiques, oddities and a bit of auction glory. Danny is on home turf and seems to know half the county, but Roo is not about to let local advantage steal the show. But what will make the money? Roo takes a fancy to something with a sporting swing, though she will be hoping to avoid any bogies. Danny has his eye on a cracking little curiosity with more than a hint of egg about it and grapples with a sizeable garden ornament. Along the way, the pair get wrapped up in an ancient Japanese textile art form and meet the woman who is trying to bring this dying craft back from the brink. All roads lead to Windsor, where a Thames-side auction decides who has played a blinder.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The Beechgrove garden is situated on an exposed Aberdeenshire hillside and is often regarded as a litmus test for what you are able to grow in Scotland. In this episode, we meet gardeners in Orkney, Shetland and the Black Isle who laugh at Beechgrove’s so-called difficult conditions as they show how they have created the most stunning sites right on the very edges of Scotland.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The Great British Sewing Bee does its bit for the planet with Reduce, Reuse and Recycle week. Host Sara Pascoe invites the nine remaining home sewers to create a quilted patchwork jacket from a load of old scraps from past Sewing Bees. Next, in the Transformation Challenge, the sewers breathe new life into boring old coats by completely deconstructing them and refashioning them into brand new stylish outerwear. For the Made to Measure, the sewers fit a maxi dress to a model using only an unwanted duvet cover. Who will ace this creative brief and win Garment of the Week, and who will have to leave the sewing room?

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Stephen Watson brings you all the action from the Boris Paichadze National Stadium in Tbilisi as Northern Ireland begin their UEFA Nations League campaign. Michael O'Neill's side open their League B campaign with a testing trip to Georgia. With Hungary and Ukraine also lying in wait, a win in Tbilisi would provide Northern Ireland with early momentum in the race for promotion. Can they make the perfect start? Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, while Stuart Dallas, Jim Magilton and Caragh Hamilton provide expert analysis in the studio.

programme.title: Newsnight

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The whole team are at Beechgrove Garden to mark the very last episode of 2026 and the end of the summer growing season. Although the series is almost over, there Is always gardening work to be done and enjoy, so every presenter has a tip, a task or a handy hint that can be done going into the autumn and winter. There’s a review of how the garden has coped with the changeable summer weather of this year, from very dry conditions to occasional heavy showers, and of course, George Anderson has the secateurs out for some seasonal pruning. As it’s the last episode, there Is also some judging to be done as Carole Baxter reviews the presenter plots - each planted to appeal to one of the senses - and picks a winner.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Autumn is in the air at Longmeadow, and with cooler and wetter days ahead, Monty is lifting plants to protect them during the winter months. He is also checking on the cuttings that will help shape next year's garden. Looking ahead, he plants up colourful autumn bulbs in containers and keeps a watchful eye on his ripening pumpkins. Carol Klein reveals the results of her border experiment, demonstrating how it’s possible to grow flowers and edibles side by side in a single small plot, avoiding a compromise on taste and beauty. Frances Tophill meets plantsman James Hitchmough in his private garden in Somerset to learn more about how he is developing a planting palette for a changing climate. There's a secret urban garden in Bristol bursting with bold planting and vibrant colour, plus a remarkable community group whose thriving garden is helping cultivate connections, confidence and friendship in Sheffield.
